case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that removing a child from a parent's custody because of the racial composition of the parent's household violates the Equal Protection Clause, and reversed the custody change.
key_cases.relevance: Palmore is the governing federal standard when a South Carolina placement or custody decision is alleged to rest on race, and forbids an agency or court from ratifying community prejudice through a best-interests rationale.
key_cases.quote: Private biases may be outside the reach of the law, but the law cannot, directly or indirectly, give them effect.

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Mother Ex Rel. Minor Child
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding among other things that DSS complied with the family court's order to provide the mother services tailored to her disabilities by making the referrals it did.
key_cases.relevance: It is the closest South Carolina authority on a disability-based challenge to the adequacy of reunification services, and sets a referral-based standard rather than an outcome-based one.
key_cases.quote: Even if Mother properly preserved this issue, we find DSS properly provided specialized services to Mother.

key_cases.case_name: Beattie v. Aiken County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents whose case was closed as unfounded may not examine the DSS case file, that 'report' covers all investigative information and the reporter's identity is never disclosable, and that FOIA requires separation and release of non-exempt material where a court is asked to conduct that review.
key_cases.relevance: The parents alleged the report was fabricated in retaliation for whistleblowing, and Beattie holds that even so they cannot reach the file.
key_cases.quote: The clear language of § 20-7-650 prohibits the disclosure of the DSS case file to Appellants or to anyone else.

key_cases.case_name: M. L. B. v. S. L. J.
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed, holding a State may not condition an indigent parent's appeal from a decree terminating her parental rights on prepayment of record preparation fees.
key_cases.relevance: M.L.B. is the controlling federal standard when a practice burdens indigent parents' access to review: the State may not use a parent's poverty to bar her appeal from a termination decree, and the Court rests that holding on due process and equal protection together.
key_cases.quote: Mississippi may not deny M. L. B., because of her poverty, appellate review of the sufficiency of the evidence on which the trial court found her unfit to remain a parent
